sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Spring Batch interview questions cover the batch-processing framework that powers reconciliation, ETL and reporting jobs in every regulated Java backend — the Job/Step/Tasklet/Chunk model, ItemReader/Processor/Writer, restart and skip logic, partitioning and parallel steps, JobRepository internals, and the integration patterns that show up in finance and telco interviews. Each answer leads with the framework concept, then the operational concern interviewers really want to hear.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Batch = **Job → Step → Tasklet | Chunk(reader / processor / writer)**.

- **Chunk** processing reads N, processes N, writes N — atomically per chunk.
- **`JobRepository`** persists status — restart picks up from the last good chunk.
- **Skip / retry** policies on transient errors.
- **Partitioning** for parallel steps; **remote chunking** for distributed.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:

- **Batch error handling** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.

- **Scenario-based** — applied questions tying multiple topics together. Drill these *last*, after the fundamentals are sharp.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Idempotency** — the same input must be safe to re-run; use natural keys + upsert.
- **Restart vs rerun** — restart resumes; rerun starts fresh — both are first-class.
- **Reader pagination** — never load everything; `JpaPagingItemReader` / cursor reader.
- **`@StepScope` / `@JobScope`** — late binding for run-time params (`#{jobParameters['date']}`).
- **Scheduler integration** — Quartz for complex cron, `@Scheduled` for simple.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd model this as <job> with a <chunk-oriented> step (size N tuned to <DB latency / payload size>), drive idempotency by <natural key + upsert>, allow skip on <classified transient errors>, and partition by <date / tenant> if the volume justifies it. The schedule sits behind <Quartz | @Scheduled>."*
